title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes. It sets up linear-algebraic preliminaries for A-linear categories over a general base ring A, not a field. The previous page's margin says to avoid finiteness hypotheses and speak of 'locally free of finite rank over Spec A'. The aim is to compare an A-linear category C with module categories over the endomorphism ring of a strict generator. The previous page calls this comparison the 'pseudo-saturated' category C_sp(1).

(1) Tensor products with projective modules.
- Data: X is an object of C with a left action O -> End(X) of an A-algebra O, and P is a right O-module, projective of finite type. Write P^ = Hom_O(P, O) for the dual, a left O-module.
- If P (x)_O X exists, i.e. it corepresents Y |-> Hom_O(P, Hom(X, Y)), there is a canonical left-O-linear evaluation map P^ -> Hom(P (x)_O X, X).
- By adjunction this gives a morphism of contravariant functors on C: P (x)_O X -> Hom_O(P^, X). Here Hom_O(P^, X) is the presheaf Y |-> Hom_O(P^, Hom(Y, X)).
- Since P is finitely generated projective, Hom_O(P^, M) = P (x)_O M. So the target is Y |-> P (x)_O Hom(Y, X).
- The tensor product 'exists in the strict sense' when this map is an isomorphism. Then P (x)_O X both corepresents Hom_O(P, Hom(X, -)) and represents P (x)_O Hom(-, X); it is the absolute, Cauchy-type tensor.
- 'Tensor products in C are reasonable' means: whenever P is f.g. projective, P (x)_O X exists, and it does so strictly.
- The bracketed remark: if C is additive and Karoubian, this holds automatically. Write P as the image of an idempotent e on O^n; then P (x)_O X is the image of e acting on X^n, which is strict.
- Grothendieck notes it suffices to require this for O = End(X), since P (x)_O X = (P (x)_O End X) (x)_{End X} X.
- Then P |-> P (x)_O X is fully faithful on the f.g. projective P for which P (x)_O X exists. This is the additive Yoneda / Morita statement: Hom(P (x) X, P' (x) X) = Hom_O(P, P'), reduced to P = O^n.
- Hence add(X), the Karoubian additive closure of X in C, is equivalent to the category of f.g. projective right End(X)-modules.

(2) Definition of a 'jolie' category (a crossed-out earlier name is unreadable). C is jolie if:
- tensor products in C are reasonable; and
- for any two objects X, X', Hom(X, X') is a projective module of finite type over O' = End(X') (acting by composition), and admits O = End(X) as its commutant. This is a double-centralizer / balancedness condition.

The page breaks off at: 'If C admits a strict generator X_0 (every object ...'. Presumably this continues to the conclusion of the previous page: the embedding C -> C_sp(1) = f.g. projective End(X_0)-modules.

Purpose. These are axioms for 'linear' categories over a base ring A that behave like categories of projective modules. They are a precursor to Tannakian formalism over a base, i.e. motives with coefficients in A rather than a field.
errors: As written, the 'jolie' condition cannot hold for all pairs X, X'. For X' = 0, Hom(X, 0) = 0 has commutant 0, not End(X). The same failure occurs whenever X' does not 'see' X (e.g. Hom = 0 between nonzero objects). Presumably X' should be restricted to a generator, or to nonzero objects in a suitably indecomposable or semisimple situation. The double-centralizer clause is clearly a first draft.

The direction of the module structures is loosely stated. Hom(X, X') is naturally a left End(X')-module and a right End(X)-module. Which side is meant to be projective, and over which ring, is ambiguous in the manuscript ('comme module sur O'').

The 'strict existence' condition is automatically satisfied once P (x)_O X exists in the corepresenting sense and P is f.g. projective, if C is additive and Karoubian. The distinction only matters for non-Karoubian or non-additive C, which is presumably why Grothendieck states it.

ideas.what: Tensor product P (x)_O X of an object with an O-action by a f.g. projective module, defined by (co)representability, with a 'strict' version comparing to Hom_O(P^, -)
ideas.modern_name: Tensoring/copowers by f.g. projective modules; absolute (Cauchy) colimits in A-linear categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard Morita / enriched category theory (Street, Kelly, 'Cauchy completion', 1970s-80s); in the motivic context Saavedra Rivano 1972 and Deligne-Milne 1982
ideas.where_published: Similar constructions appear in Saavedra's 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1972), which developed Grothendieck's program; not in EGA/SGA as such

ideas.what: For O = End(X), P |-> P (x)_O X is fully faithful on f.g. projective modules
ideas.modern_name: Additive Yoneda lemma / Morita equivalence add(X) = proj(End(X))

ideas.what: 'Catégorie jolie': reasonable tensor products, Hom modules f.g. projective over endomorphism rings, with double-centralizer property; strict generator X_0 giving an embedding into projective End(X_0)-modules
ideas.modern_name: Linear categories over a base ring with a projective generator; Morita-type / Tannakian categories over a ring
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972) for Tannakian categories over fields and partly over rings; later Wedhorn, Schäppi, Lurie for Tannakian theory over rings

missed.claim: This is an early (1965) draft of axioms for A-linear motivic categories over an arbitrary base ring. It uses projectivity of Hom modules plus a double-centralizer condition in place of field-based semisimplicity. It shows Grothendieck explicitly intended the motivic Galois formalism to work over Spec A with locally free coefficients, a generality only treated later (Saavedra partially, then Wedhorn/Schäppi). The axiom system itself is unfinished and partly inconsistent as stated.
missed.quote: "les produits tensoriels y sont raisonnables" et si pour deux objets X, X', Hom(X,X') comme module sur O' est projectif de t.f. et admet O' comme commutant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents the origin of Tannakian-over-a-ring ideas in Grothendieck's own 1965 notes. Mathematically the content is standard Morita theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard Morita / additive Yoneda material and a draft axiom set. Its only notable aspect is historical: Grothendieck in 1965 aimed at motivic Galois theory over a general base ring with a double-centralizer axiom. This is a modest, unsurprising detail of the record.
transcription_corrections: 'On dit que le produit tensoriel existe en {+P⊗_O X+} [?] strict' should read roughly 'On dit que le produit tensoriel P⊗_O X existe au sens strict si la flèche précédente est un isom.'
'homomorphisme [?] O-linéaire {+(gauche)+} [?] canonique' is plausibly 'homomorphisme O-linéaire (à gauche) canonique'.

The left marginal note reads 'P⊗_O X existe, et pleinement fidèle', with an arrow to the sentence 'Alors le foncteur P ↦ P⊗_O X sur la sous-catégorie des P proj. de t.f. tels que [P⊗_O X existe] est pleinement fidèle'.
Another left marginal note reads 'conditions entendues' (or similar), attached to the Karoubian remark.
'dès que [?] P est [-projectif-]' is followed by a crossed-out phrase; the intended text is 'dès que P est projectif de type fini'.
The double-centralizer clause probably reads 'Hom(X,X') comme module sur O' est projectif de t.f. et admet O comme commutant' (O, not O'). The image's interlinear 'o'' marks the module ring.
The supplied NEXT PAGE transcription (holomorphic functions, '- 34 -') is clearly from an unrelated typescript and does not continue this page.
